evals.prompt: Extract a full design system from this dark editorial product screenshot and return it as YAML.
evals.expected_output: One parser-valid YAML document holding every canonical section in schema order, with not-applicable objects wherever the screenshot carries no evidence.
assertions: The response contains YAML only, with no markdown fences and no surrounding prose.
Every canonical top-level section appears in the schema order.
Unsupported layers use an object with applicability, confidence, and inference_basis rather than null.
The validator was run before the document was returned.

evals.prompt: Choose the typefaces for this poster system. They must be rare Google Fonts.
evals.expected_output: Selected families drawn from the live Google Fonts catalog during the run, each carrying a complete rarity record at or above the floor.
assertions: The live catalog is read during the run rather than recalled from memory.
Each selected family records popularity rank, total families, rarity percentile, trending rank, date added, source, and retrieval date.
No selected family is a common interface default.
The rarity explanation cites the measured rank instead of relying on adjectives.

evals.prompt: This hero image is all I have. Tell me the brand meaning and the motion system too.
evals.expected_output: Observed facts, inferred logic, and speculative extrapolation kept in separate buckets, with brand meaning and motion marked as inference or speculation.
assertions: Directly visible facts stay in the observed bucket.
Brand meaning and motion behavior are labelled as inference or speculation.
Each extrapolated value names the visual cue behind it in inference_basis.
An observed typeface is recorded separately from a selected family.

evals.prompt: Build the design system for a moody fintech app. Nothing is attached and the network is down.
evals.expected_output: A stop-and-report answer that asks for a reference, states that live rarity cannot be measured, and names the failed command.
assertions: The response asks for a visual reference instead of inventing a system.
The response states that the live catalog is unreachable and that rarity cannot be verified.
The response names the exact command or source that failed.
No rarity record is filled from memory or from an older snapshot.

evals.prompt: Validate this extraction file I already have and tell me what is wrong with it.
evals.expected_output: A fresh validator run whose reported problems are quoted, with each fix named against the failing path.
assertions: The validator is run against the supplied file rather than judged by reading.
Reported problems are quoted from the fresh run, including any font rule failures.
A stale popularity rank is reported as drift against the live catalog.
The answer states the exit code rather than claiming validity from memory.
